## Major Update: Constants Are Derived
The Lemniscate-Alpha program proposes a compact set of relations connecting many constants to four integers: b₃=7, N_c=3, N_eff=13, N_base=4. Where a relation is derived vs. identified vs. companion-work is indicated in the tables.
:::

These are the true inputs from which everything else follows.

| Integer | Value | Physical Origin | Role |
|---------|-------|-----------------|------|
| b₃ | 7 | QCD beta function coefficient | Gauge structure |
| N_c | 3 | Number of color charges | SU(3) |
| N_eff | 13 | Effective dimension (Fibonacci F₇) | Scaling |
| N_base | 4 | Base harmonic modes | Wave structure |

![Derivation chain showing how the four framework integers produce the derived constants.](../../media/images/fig-constants-graph.png){#fig-constants-graph}

**Self-consistency**: These satisfy the master quadratic:
$$
x^2 - 16(G^*)^2 x + 16(G^*)^3 = 0
$$
where $G^* = 2.9587$ is the FTD-derived lemniscatic constant (not Gauss's classical constant ≈ 2.622; see @sec-glossary).

### Proton Mass: Two Paths to the Same Number

The proton-to-electron mass ratio admits two independent derivations that converge through G*.

#### Pure Geometry Path (π-based)

$$
\frac{m_p}{m_e} = 6\pi^5 = 1836.118 \quad \text{(0.002\% error)}
$$

This uses only the integer 6 and π, with no framework integers or G*.

#### Framework Integer Path

$$
\frac{m_p}{m_e} = \frac{N_{\text{eff}}}{\alpha} + T(10) = \frac{13}{1/137.036} + 55 = 1836.47 \quad \text{(0.017\% error)}
$$

Where T(10) = 55 is the 10th triangular number.

#### The Connection: Why Both Work

$$
6\pi^5 \approx (G^*)^7 \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{N_{\text{eff}}}\right) = (G^*)^7 \times \frac{12}{13}
$$

Both formulas converge because the lemniscatic constant G* encodes the relationship between circular geometry (π) and framework integers. The factor (1 - 1/N_eff) = 12/13 connects the pure-π formula to the integer-based one.

| Path | Formula | Predicted | Measured | Error |
|------|---------|-----------|----------|-------|
| Pure $\pi$ | $6\pi^5$ | 1836.118 | 1836.153 | 0.002% |
| Framework integers | $N_{eff}/\alpha + T(10)$ | 1836.47 | 1836.153 | 0.017% |
